assertion.statement: For every B in the stated pole-completeness domain, one common positive signed divisor m of2730 gives A=mB,H=A(A-B^2), with positive squarefree classes beta congruent17 mod24 and theta congruent1 mod24. There exist positive squarefree n,n theta congruent11 mod12 for which the full multiplication-by-two Selmer groups have dimension3 and contain the same extra class(beta,1).
assertion.objects: The same B,m,A,H,beta,theta; support matrices K,s,lambda and the two actual elliptic curves E_n,E_(n theta), in Kummer coordinates(x+3ell,x-ell).
assertion.hypotheses: B has square reduced denominator,0<B<1/2 and v_p(B)>=4 for p in{2,3,5,7,13}; retain the split-cubic Kummer map, odd local formal-group calculation, local squareclass and reciprocity facts, CRT and Dirichlet.
assertion.quantifiers: For every such B choose m first, then beta,theta; construct one compatible auxiliary-prime assignment for both supports before selecting the actual primes.
assertion.parameter_range: beta>1,theta>=1 are coprime positive squarefree and prime to6; all auxiliary primes are distinct and avoid6 beta theta.
assertion.uniformity: The block determinant argument works for arbitrary d=omega(beta)>=1 and every finite theta support; no finite matrix test substitutes for it.
assertion.constants: The original2730 multiplier catalogue and old-prime valuation4 remain fixed; exactly d-1 I slots plus one q0 slot are used.
assertion.normalizations: Retain actual nonzero beta/theta cross-symbols and their two zero row sums; Ksharp=K+lambda a^t; q0 deletion and full-product determinant coefficient1. Selmer means full2-Selmer, not isogeny Selmer.
assertion.exceptional_cases: d=1 has empty I block; theta=1 permits identical two parameters. Necessary dyadic conditions give only an upper bound; the particular(beta,1) is separately checked locally at every place and independent of rational2-torsion.
assertion.limit_order: Reconcile all Legendre and local conditions before CRT/Dirichlet. Establish exact finite Selmer dimension before full-corank deduction or either use of RC; no rational point or finite Sha inferred here.
